source.paper: Northcutt, Athalye, Mueller (2021), Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks, NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks; labelerrors.com

ground_truth.confirmed: candidate with mturk.given < 3 (fewer than 3 of 5 workers chose the given label alone). Reproduces the paper's counts exactly: 54 (CIFAR-10), 585 (CIFAR-100), 15 (MNIST). Tried first and rejected for not matching: given+both < 3 (37, 465, 15), which is what 'a majority did not accept the given label' would suggest; guessed+neither >= 3 gives 38/486/18 as given<guessed+neither and 18/318/23 as guessed>=3. The definition was chosen by matching published counts, not by any detector result.
ground_truth.all_candidates: every candidate cleanlab flagged, unverified (secondary ground truth)
ground_truth.caveat: Positives are only found among cleanlab's candidates (confident learning on a different model), so precision is a lower bound (unflagged errors count as clean) and the candidate set favours confident-learning-style detectors.

order_check: the test labels torchvision loads must equal original_test_labels exactly (asserted); ids index test-set rows
embedding: ResNet-18 ImageNet penultimate layer (app.detection.image_embed), pixel features and PCA(32) fitted on reference rows, as bench_mm.prepare_batch; MNIST grey replicated to 3 channels

mode_a_reference.reference: stratified random sample of the TRAINING set (clean labels)
mode_a_reference.incoming: the whole test set in seeded random order, scored in chunks of batch_rows; every image gets one row score
mode_a_reference.detector: app.detection.veritas_mm.detect (class_signature on, as for images); reported: veritas_mm row scores and the label check alone

mode_b_no_reference.detector: app.detection.veritas_mm.self_check on the test set in seeded random order; score = 'label' list rows

metrics.app_list: per chunk the top min(200, max(20, 5% of chunk)) rows; recall and precision of the union

policy: No tuning on these results. Nothing is planted. Run once and quote the numbers as they come; any change to the detector or definitions means a new benchmark_id.
